source.title: How does Weight Correlation Affect the Generalisation Ability of Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Gao Jin; Xin-Ping Yi; Liang Zhang; Li-Jun Zhang; S. Schewe; Xiaowei Huang

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a weight-correlation regularizer and weight-correlation-based measures relate to generalization error, using methods distinct from the mapped claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports WCD comparisons and per-network weight-correlation and generalization-error measurements. Cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows. The versions' specific interventions or measures are not tested.
record.test_reason: Table 3 reports held-out classification errors for fully connected and convolutional networks trained from scratch with SGD, bearing on V3. Isolating local connectivity is unnecessary to test its architecture comparison, although these experiments cannot establish that mechanism. Weight correlation and constant-variance PAC-Bayes measures do not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors argue that weight correlation helps explain generalization, improves their PAC-Bayes complexity ranking, and supplies an effective regularizer. Their abstract and introduction make stronger improvement claims than the mixed experimental results warrant; the record appropriately acknowledges small improvements and exceptions.
record.recipe_differences: Studies a weight-correlation regularizer and correlation-aware complexity measures; it does not reproduce the claim versions' specified interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: WCD error outcomes vary by dataset and architecture: results on MNIST include an increase and an unchanged error; on CIFAR-10, SVHN, CIFAR-100 and Caltech-256, several reported decreases are small and one CIFAR-100 result increases.

fits_no_version.finding: WCD changes held-out errors, usually modestly improving them, with increases on MNIST VGG16* and CIFAR-100 VGG16* and unchanged errors in some cases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-correlation regularization can improve classification performance, depending on architecture and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: The correlation-aware PBC measure has Kendall's tau 0.61 on CIFAR-10 and 0.55 on CIFAR-100, exceeding the compared measures. Its variance is fixed rather than estimated through perturbation tolerance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding weight correlation to the tested PAC-Bayes complexity measure improves its ranking of loss generalization gaps across these architectures.

record.peer_reviewed: 34th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2020)
record.problems: The measure-ranking experiments use a small set of architectures on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. The paper notes ambiguous MNIST results and that some datasets have high errors because the networks are small. It uses early stopping and reports best loss and corresponding error across final training epochs. No random-label capability check is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 and Table 6 also report loss, training loss and WC for the WCD comparisons; these measures were left out to keep the extraction within the row limit while retaining each reported test-error comparison. Table 4 reports CIFAR-100 complexity measures and rankings; these were not extracted. Table 2 and Table 4 also report individual complexity-measure values (PFN, PSN, NoP, SoSP, PB and PBC), concordant and discordant pairs, and Kendall's τ; only the individual GE and WC values from Table 2 were retained. Table 3 and Table 6 locators identify the reported comparisons.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label accuracy, and random-label held-out chance performance.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error threshold.

The causal contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse local connections, and initialization from trained convolutional networks. No held-out classification-error comparison of FCNs and CNNs is supplied for CIFAR-100.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and effects of tuning or optimizer modifications.
Batch-size interventions and their interaction with epoch budgets and training recipes.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures; Section 6.1 explicitly uses constant variance instead of sharpness estimation.
Removal of memorized examples versus random removals.

record.verdict_notes: V3 verdicts use cross-architecture comparisons of the errors already retained in Table 3 rows, including their baseline values, rather than the within-architecture WCD differences. Appendix G specifies SGD with learning rate 0.01, 100 FCN epochs and 500 CNN epochs; matched training loss applies within WCD pairs, not across architectures. These comparisons do not isolate architectural causation. Reported ±0.5 percentage points are not identified as a particular uncertainty statistic.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not compared.
No width sweep around the zero-training-error threshold is reported.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks isolates local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers are not compared with SGD.
Batch size and its interaction with training duration or recipe are not tested.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness is not measured or compared with norm- and margin-based measures.
Memorized examples are not identified, removed, or compared with random removals.
